samples.summary: The new `MAX_FONT_SIZE` / `MAX_LINE_HEIGHT` bands are fully bypassable through the unvalidated, peer-writable `stylesJson` named-style registry, which reaches the identical line-height sink
samples.evidence:
`docsTreeToDocument` does a bare `JSON.parse(opts.stylesJson)` into `doc.styles` with no schema validation (crdt-tree.ts:309-315). `resolveStyleBlock` then spreads that object verbatim (`named-styles.ts:284`), `effectiveBlockSpacing` uses `styleBlock?.lineHeight` raw (`named-styles.ts:639-641`), and `resolveBlockInlines` merges the registry's `inline.fontSize` as the base layer of EVERY run (`layout.ts:165-172`), which `getLineMaxFontSizePx` turns into the line height (`layout.ts:1056-1075`, `assignLineHeights` at 874-888).

Attack: a collaborator (or an API key with write scope) sets `stylesJson` to `{"normal":{"inline":{"fontSize":1e9},"block":{"lineHeight":1e9}}}`. `normalizeFontSize` (ceiling 400) and `normalizeLineHeight` (ceiling 20) are never consulted on this path, so every reader lays every paragraph out at a ~1e9 px line height — the exact million-page/row-height amplification the diff exists to prevent, now only partially absorbed by `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` (200 pages *per table row*). Non-numeric values are worse: `Math.max(1, "abc")` is `NaN` (named-styles.ts:874), giving `NaN` line heights and a blank document for every reader — the harm the diff cites as its justification for `computeTableLayout` step 5d.

The REST arm is reachable too: `assertValidDocsBody` (docs-content.controller.ts:295-316) validates `blocks`/`header`/`footer` and never inspects `styles`, and `writeDocsRoot` stores it verbatim (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:350`). A finite `1e9` survives `JSON.stringify` intact, so a single authenticated `PUT` poisons the document for every subsequent reader.
searchedFor: read docs-content.controller.ts assertValidDocsBody for a `styles` validator

samples.summary: `rowSpan` / `colSpan` are still read through a bare `Number(...)` at both hardened boundaries and drive an unbounded fixed-point loop — a peer-written `rowSpan="Infinity"` hangs the tab of anyone who selects cells in that table
samples.evidence:
Both read boundaries the change hardened leave the spans raw: `crdt-tree.ts:187-188` and `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:452-453` (`colSpan: attrs.colSpan ? Number(attrs.colSpan) : undefined`). `normalizeTableMerges` — the only clamp for out-of-grid spans — runs solely in the paste sanitizer (`clipboard.ts:351`) and the table-insert paths (`text-editor.ts:4440,4472`), never on the CRDT read path (verified by grep).

Sink: `expandCellRangeForMerges` (`packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:66-91`) grows the rect from the span with no clamp to the table's real dimensions — `const r2 = r + rspan - 1; if (r2 > rowEnd) { rowEnd = r2; changed = true; }` (lines 77-80). With `rspan = Infinity`, `rowEnd` becomes `Infinity` and `for (let r = rowStart; r <= rowEnd; r++)` never terminates: a permanent main-thread hang. A large finite span (`1e9`) freezes for tens of seconds instead. It is reached from ordinary gestures — drag/shift-arrow cell selection (`text-editor.ts:2339,2359,3296`), `table-merge-context.ts:53` — and from `normalizeCellRange` (`selection.ts:112`), which runs on every render of a range that has a `tableCellRange`, so once the selection exists the hang recurs on each repaint. Same threat model, same two boundaries, no band.
searchedFor: grep rowSpan|colSpan in packages/docs/src/model and view

samples.summary: The table `cols` attribute is unbanded at the same read boundary: unbounded column count drives an O(rows × cols) allocation loop, and `Infinity`/mixed-sign ratios produce the same NaN geometry step 5d was added to prevent — but 5d covers row heights only
samples.evidence:
`const cols = (attrs.cols ?? '').split(',').map(Number).filter((n) => !isNaN(n))` (crdt-tree.ts:209-212; identical in `yorkie-doc-store.ts` around line 466) accepts any count and any magnitude — `Number('1e400')` is `Infinity`, which passes `!isNaN`.

(a) Amplification: `numCols = columnWidths.length` drives `computeTableLayout`'s nested `for r < numRows / for c < numCols` loop, allocating a `LayoutTableCell` (plus a default line array) per iteration (`table-layout.ts:170-201`) regardless of how many cells the row actually has. A single ~2 MB `cols` attribute (1e6 entries) plus a few dozen rows is tens of millions of allocations — an OOM/freeze for every reader from one cheap write.

(b) Poisoned geometry: `columnPixelWidths = columnWidths.map(ratio => ratio * contentWidth)` (table-layout.ts:157) yields `Infinity`, and a `cols="1e400,-1e400"` spanned cell makes `cellWidth` `NaN` (line 187) → `totalWidth`/`columnXOffsets` NaN → the table draws nothing. The change added step 5d specifically because "a NaN row height … blanks the table for every reader" (table-layout.ts:303-322) but published no equivalent guarantee for `columnPixelWidths` / `totalWidth`, which the renderers, hit-tests and selection math read just as raw.
searchedFor: read clipboard.ts sanitizeTableData (paste path derives cols from real cells)

samples.summary: `isPaintableImageSize` drops rather than clamps above the ceiling, so an already-stored legitimate image larger than 20000 px silently disappears from the model on read and can be erased from the CRDT by the next write-back
samples.evidence: `isPaintableImageSize` returns false for `width > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE || height > MAX_IMAGE_SIZE`, and both read boundaries then skip building `style.image` entirely (crdt-tree.ts:97-105; yorkie-doc-store.ts:215-222). Unlike the other bands, this converts an out-of-band value into *content loss* rather than a clamp: no insert path bounds image height (the branch's own notes concede a narrow-and-tall image "silently vanishes on the next read"), and any operation that re-materializes the block from the parsed model (block split/merge, `setDocument`) persists the image-free version — an integrity/availability regression against existing documents, not just a rendering choice. A proportional clamp (as the deferred follow-up suggests) preserves the same DoS bound without destroying content.

samples.summary: `MAX_ROW_PAGE_SPAN` bounds a single row only; there is no global cap on emitted pages, so a hostile table still amplifies one small write into a very large page/PageLine allocation
samples.evidence: The bound is applied per row inside the `for (let ri = 0; ri < tl.rowHeights.length; ri++)` loop (pagination.ts:122-191). With `rowHeights` banded to `MAX_ROW_HEIGHT` (10000 px) against a ~864 px content box, each row still yields ~12 pages, and a content-derived height (banded `fontSize` 400 pt × `lineHeight` 20 ≈ 10.6k px per line) can reach the full 200 fragments per row. A table of a few hundred rows therefore still produces tens of thousands of `LayoutPage`/`PageLine` objects from a modest write — a large constant-factor amplification the per-row bound does not address. Hardening only; termination itself is correctly guaranteed.

samples.summary: The docs arm of the v1 content validator recurses into nested table cells with no depth ceiling, unlike the slides arm's `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` — a deeply nested payload stack-overflows the validator on an authenticated endpoint
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` recurses `assertValidBlock(cell.blocks[cb], …)` (docs-content.controller.ts:469-474) with no depth parameter, while the slides walk explicitly bounds itself at `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` (line 727) for exactly this reason ("the JSON body limit is 25 MB — enough for a compact payload to exhaust the stack on an authenticated endpoint"). The same unbounded recursion exists on the read side in `treeNodeToBlock` → `treeNodeToRow` → `treeNodeToCell` (crdt-tree.ts:169-233), so a peer-written deeply nested table also blows the stack in every reader's parse. Out of diff and pre-existing, but it is the same untrusted-structure class the change is hardening, and the clipboard sanitizer's `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` shows the intended bound exists nowhere on the CRDT/REST paths.

verdict.reason: The named-style registry is an unvalidated, peer- and API-writable input that reaches the same font-size/line-height geometry sinks the MAX_FONT_SIZE/MAX_LINE_HEIGHT bands protect, and no band is applied anywhere on that path. Verified each link: crdt-tree.ts:309-315 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:687-696 both JSON.parse the blob with only a cast (no schema check); resolveStyleInline (named-styles.ts:261-274) and resolveStyleBlock (280-285) spread the registry verbatim; effectiveBlockSpacing (602-641) applies its finiteness guard `authoredOr` only to the block's own value, returning `styleBlock?.lineHeight` raw; assignLineHeights (layout.ts:873-888) then does Math.max(1, lineHeight) * getLineMaxFontSizePx (1056-1075) with no ceiling, so 1e9 passes and "abc" yields NaN heights. A repo-wide grep for normalizeFontSize/normalizeLineHeight shows call sites only at attribute boundaries (crdt-attrs.ts:169, crdt-tree.ts:83, clipboard.ts:166/222, yorkie-doc-store.ts:200) and none for DocStyles. The REST arm is reachable: assertValidDocsBody (docs-content.controller.ts:295-316) inspects only blocks/header/footer, the handler takes `@Body() body: unknown` (line 158) so the global whitelist ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-72) cannot strip `styles`, and writeDocsRoot (backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:349-352) persists it verbatim. Caveat recorded but not refuting: for non-table blocks paginateLayout (pagination.ts:196-216) emits at most one page per oversized line, so the "million page" amplification is overstated outside tables; the NaN/blank-render and unbanded geometry remain.

verdict.reason: Verified independently; no counterexample exists. Both CRDT read boundaries read spans raw (crdt-tree.ts:187-188, yorkie-doc-store.ts:452-453) while sibling attributes at the same boundaries ARE banded (normalizeCellPadding crdt-tree.ts:146, normalizeRowHeight crdt-tree.ts:220 / yorkie-doc-store.ts:474, with comments naming non-terminating loops as the motive). The only out-of-grid span clamp, normalizeTableMerges (types.ts:692, clamp at 726-727), has exactly three callers — clipboard.ts:351 (paste sanitizer) and text-editor.ts:4440,4472 (table insert) — none on the CRDT read path; the backend writer docs-tree.ts:117-120 only stringifies spans without validating. The sink is genuinely unbounded: expandCellRangeForMerges (selection.ts:56-98) sets rowEnd = r + rspan - 1 at 77-80 with no bound against the table's dimensions and re-scans `for (r = rowStart; r <= rowEnd; r++)` at :68; with rspan = Infinity the loop never terminates since missing cells merely continue at :71. Every other span consumer clamps (table-layout.ts:226,277; table-renderer.ts:161,598; table-geometry.ts:46; and even selection.ts:665 in the same file), isolating 77-80 as the sole unbounded read. The layout path tolerates an Infinity span, so the hostile table renders and its cells stay selectable, and the loop is reached from ordinary gestures: drag cell-range selection (text-editor.ts:2339,2359,3296), merge menu (table-merge-context.ts:53), and normalizeCellRange (selection.ts:112) via normalizeRange (:126), which runs on every getNormalizedRange/computeSelectionRects for a range carrying a tableCellRange — including remote peer selection painting, so the hang recurs each repaint. Existing tests (cell-range-expand.test.ts:58-115) cover only in-grid spans. In lane as untrusted-input handling: a peer-controlled Tree attribute reaching an unbounded loop is an availability DoS, the same threat model the adjacent banded attributes were hardened against.

verdict.reason: The absence is real and I could not find any counterexample. crdt-tree.ts:209-212 parses `cols` with only `!isNaN`, which admits Infinity, negative magnitudes and an unbounded entry count, and assigns it straight to `tableData.columnWidths` (line 229) while the sibling `rowHeights` on lines 217-221 is banded via `normalizeRowHeight`. The frontend reader repeats the same expression (yorkie-doc-store.ts:467) and its writer serializeTableAttrs (yorkie-doc-store.ts:349-358) does no finiteness filtering, unlike serializeBlockStyleAttrs (crdt-attrs.ts:94-99). In computeTableLayout, numCols = columnWidths.length drives the nested r/c allocation loop (table-layout.ts:153,170-201) irrespective of real cell count, columnPixelWidths (157), cellWidth (184-187) and totalWidth (345) are consumed raw, and the newly added step 5d (318-322) bands rowHeights only. No column band exists elsewhere: no MAX_COL* constant in the repo, numeric-attrs.ts/row-height.ts/list-level.ts cover other attributes only, normalizeTableMerges (types.ts:692-731) clamps spans only, the paste sanitizer derives cols from real cells (clipboard.ts:307-333) so it does not cover the CRDT path, and the server-side validator checks only Array.isArray(columnWidths) (docs-content.controller.ts:449-450) before docs-tree.ts:155 joins it into the attribute. Downstream consumers (table-renderer.ts:132,291, table-geometry.ts:157, table-resize.ts:48, text-editor.ts:5137) read the geometry without re-validating, so one cheap write by a doc collaborator or API writer degrades every reader — the same untrusted-attribute hardening class the adjacent guards were written for, left uncovered on the column axis.
